ExplanationParts.CorpusEarnedOpening: To pass the barrier is to get through a tested obstruction: the records contrast those already through with those still stopped, and extend the phrase to a barrier-passing eye and phrase.
EvidenceBody: Huanglong Huinan distinguishes the two conditions: 'one already past the barrier swings his arms and goes straight on' (已過關者掉臂徑去), whereas 'this is one who has not passed the barrier' (此未透關者也). Zhongfeng Mingben records a corrective contrast: people thread all old and new public cases onto one string and call it 'passing the barrier' (謂之透關), while 'the tight barrier of life and death beneath their heels has not actually been passed' (脚跟下一座生死牢關，政好不曾透得). The phrase also builds 'an eye that passes the barrier' (透關眼). Yuanwu Keqin asks whether anyone present has such an eye. Chijue Daochong says, 'Passing the barrier requires a barrier-passing eye; obtaining treasure requires one who can distinguish treasure' (透關須具透關眼，得寶須還別寶人). Poshan Haiming answers the question 'What is a phrase that passes the barrier?' (如何是透關句), and Dabian Xianquan contrasts 'one already through the barrier' (已透關者) with 'one not through the barrier' (未透關者). These are recorded descriptions, corrections, and compounds; this entry adds no unrecorded destination beyond the barrier.
